## Upgrade

- **Migration 031 adds a nullable `enqueue_leased_until` column to `event`.** Run `hot db migrate` with the 3.0.4 CLI. Events published earlier keep NULL, which means nothing is owed.

## Features

- **`POST /v1/events` takes an `event_id`, which makes a publish safe to send again.** A publish generated its own id, so a resend after a timeout or a 500 was a second event. Now a caller can name the event with a UUID of its own. A second publish with the same id, type, data and stream starts nothing new and gets the first answer. If the first publish kept the event but never reached the queue, the resend finishes it. A different event with the id gets a `409` with code `event_id_conflict`, and so does the id in another environment, because event ids are unique across environments. Publishes without an `event_id` work as before.

## Fixes

- **Repeating a schedule at its account's limit works.** Resending the same active call, or a one-time call already spent, returns its schedule ID without reserving another slot. New calls and rearming cancelled calls still need capacity.
- **Collection fields keep their checks inside mixed unions.** A `Vec<Int> | Other` field refuses `[1, "bad"]`, while a `Map<Str, Int> | Other` field accepts a valid map instead of losing that member. Another collection member or record can still match when the first alternative refuses the data.
- **Map fields check their keys too.** A `Map<Str, Int>` field refuses an integer key. Exact numeric key conversions work as at other fields; a conversion that would combine two keys returns an Err rather than dropping an entry.
- **An inline constraint resolves its named base.** With `Money type Dec`, a parameter declared `Money where gt(%, 0)` accepts `Money(5.0)` instead of failing `hot check` with “expected Money, got Dec”. Imports and namespace aliases resolve where the annotation is declared.
- **Recursive schema definitions have distinct keys.** Namespace separators and underscores could produce the same `$defs` key, so `::a_b/Tree` and `::a::b/Tree` got one type's fields. Definition names now escape punctuation, and each `$ref` names its own definition.

- **A deployment no longer strands itself when a worker starts.** Startup recovery and a deployment's queued message both work on one build. When recovery activated the build first, which a backlog of events ahead of the message made likely, the message found it already live, took that for a stale deployment, and marked the live build `superseded`. Events were then accepted and matched nothing, with no error, and a restart didn't help: only the next deploy did. Now one of them activates the build and the other leaves it alone. A live build leaves `ready` only through a new deployment. The manifest isn't loaded again over a live build, which also left a gap where events matched nothing and deactivated schedules armed since activation. A build already stranded this way comes back at the next worker start. Recovery now publishes `deploy:succeeded` too.
- **Events wait for a deployment in an environment of any size.** An event with no handler waits while a deployment is in progress, but the check read only eight builds, deployed ones first. In an environment with eight or more deployed builds it missed the deployment, and events were acknowledged as unhandled.
- **Two schedules of one function at one time both fire.** Hot kept one schedule per function and time, whatever its arguments, so a second `hot:schedule:new` due at the same moment failed with a duplicate key, and that call was lost. A schedule is now one call: a function, a time and its arguments. Sending the same call again returns the ID of the schedule it repeats instead of failing, a cancelled schedule can be armed again, and a one-time schedule that already fired stays spent. `hot test` arms a repeat the same way. Migration 030 replaces the index on both databases. Restart services with it: a build deployed through a worker of the previous version after the migration fails, and can be deployed again.
- **A name in `meta` reaches the build as its definition's full name.** The build manifest and the `meta` columns held a name as it was written, so `agent: Imported` stayed `Imported` and `::lib/Clause` kept its alias, and a nested name in a workflow's or agent's meta, such as `policy: {form: Complaint}`, became `{"$ast": "lang::Value"}`. Event handlers, schedules, webhooks, MCP tools, agents and workflows now all hold `::ns/Name`, the name the compiler already resolves. A run of a handler whose agent is imported from another namespace is now tagged with that agent, so it counts in the agent's health in the app. A path stays on the name, so `limits.port` no longer lands as plain `limits`. Builds made earlier keep the meta they stored.
- **Load order no longer decides whether a type alias is there.** A top-level value could call a function in another namespace before that namespace had run, and if the function named a type through an alias such as `Thing ::o::a/Thing`, the load stopped with `Function 'Thing' not found`, though `hot check` passed. Whether it happened depended on which namespace sorted first. Aliases of types, enums and variants, written in full or as a local alias, are now bound before any namespace runs, so this holds for namespaces that read each other's values too.
- **An agent's `mcp_servers` entry in the manifest names its server.** For an `mcp-servers` entry that's a name, `target` held a debug dump of the reference, which included the absolute path of the source file on the machine that made the build. It now holds the name, such as `::demo::flows/remote`.
- **`hot check` warns when a variant is used as its payload.** Inside an `Enum.Variant` arm the matched name is the variant, and a payload that isn't a record is reached by binding it (`Status.OpenAll (asks) =>`). Code that treated the name as the payload checked clean, then failed or got a wrong value: `map(s, key)` stopped the run, `length(s)` counted the variant's own keys, and a `Str` payload came back as the variant. The new `variant-as-payload` warning covers a call's arguments, a declared return type, annotated bindings, record fields, templates and comparisons with a literal. Fields of a record payload still read through the name.
- **`::hot::regex/capture` declares what it returns.** It was declared to return `Str`, but it returns `{match, groups}`, or null when nothing matches. Passing a bound result to a `Map` parameter stopped `hot check` with a type mismatch, and passing it to a `Str` parameter checked clean. It now declares `Map?`, and its docs describe the result.
- **A tool's schema describes its own types.** Tool and MCP schemas found a field's type by its simple name across the whole program, so two namespaces that both declare `Facts` could get each other's fields. A name now means what it means where it's written, through imports and namespace aliases, and an aliased tool reads its target's namespace. A variant's `$type` in a schema is its full name, as a value of it holds, and `$defs` entries are named by full name (with punctuation escaped).
- **A handler woken by a retry gets its own retries.** An event a retried run sent carried the sender's attempt, so its handlers started at that attempt and counted their retries from it. A handler woken by a last attempt got none. An event's handlers now start at attempt 0, whichever attempt sent it. A retry of the same handler still counts up, and `origin_run_id` is unchanged.
- **`POST /v1/events` outlasts a brief queue failure.** The API wrote the event, then tried its enqueue once. If that failed, for example through a Redis restart, the caller got a 500 and nothing ever processed the row. It now retries as a handler's `send()` does, for up to about 4 seconds, before it answers 500.
- **A git dependency pinned by `tag` gets that tag.** Hot cloned the repository shallow from its default branch, with no tags, so checking out the tag failed. The clone stayed in the cache, so the project then ran the default branch's code, with the pin still in place. A `branch` other than the default failed the same way, and so did a commit SHA. Hot now clones the ref you name, and replaces a clone an earlier release left on the wrong commit. A ref the repository doesn't have fails on every run.
- **The New Organization page creates an organization.** Its form posted `org_name` and `org_slug`, and the app expected `name` and `slug`, so every attempt answered `422 Failed to deserialize form body: missing field name`. On a self-hosted installation that stopped the first administrator right after `hot admin bootstrap`: with no organization there are no sub-organizations and no org API keys. An individual account takes its owner's name.
- **`hot app` takes `--queue.type` and the other queue flags.** Its error for a `memory` queue told you to pass `--queue.type`, which only the other services accepted.
- **Key reads say when a rotation's overlap ends.** Only the answer to `POST /v1/api-keys/{id}/rotate` said when the old secret stops working. `GET /v1/api-keys/{id}` and both key lists now report it in `previous_secret_expires_at` while the overlap runs, for org keys and environment keys, and the app shows it on the **Sub-orgs** page.
- **The app rotates org keys.** A root administrator can rotate any org key on the **Sub-orgs** page, and choose how long the old secret keeps working. Until now an org key a person made couldn't be rotated: the API rotates only keys the caller issued, and no key rotates itself.
- **`hot db migrate` names the PostgreSQL version it needs.** On PostgreSQL 17 or older it stopped at the first migration with `function uuidv7() does not exist`. It now says that Hot needs PostgreSQL 18 or newer, names the server's version, and applies nothing. [Self-Hosted PostgreSQL](/docs/configuration/postgres) states the requirement.
- **`hot deploy --local` reaches the configured build storage.** It wrote the bundle under `.hot/build` and then read it from build storage, so any other storage path, or S3 or GCS, failed with `Build file not found`. It now copies the bundle into build storage, and a remote store is recorded on the build.
- **An unpacked release archive finds its own files.** The archive keeps `db/`, `app/` and `pkg/` beside the binary, and Hot looked for a `resources/` folder, so it couldn't find its migrations, even with `HOT_HOME` set. Hot now finds them beside the binary and in `HOT_HOME`, with no linked folders.
- **A record refuses a field of the wrong type when it's built.** `Rec({n: "not an int"})` built a record for `n: Int`, and the value failed later, or never, wherever it was read. The constructor now checks each field as a parameter checks its argument, in the Map and named forms: the Err is a `ConstraintError.Violation` whose `path` names the field, through nested records and lists. It covers null at a required field, `Int?`, the contents of `Vec<T>` and `Map<K, V>`, and an enum variant's built-in payload. A record or enum field no longer wraps a plain value in a tag it doesn't fit, such as a Str at a record field.
- **An Err given for a record field stays that Err.** A record field read the Err's payload as its data, so `Outer({inner: err({value: 1})})` built an `Inner` from the payload and dropped the Err.
- **openai 1.3.1: response records say which fields OpenAI leaves null.** The generated types declared `first_id`, `completed_at`, `last_error`, `usage` and similar as required, though they're null on an empty list, a run that hasn't finished, or a job still queued. qwen 1.0.4 and openai-compatible 0.1.1 move to this version.
- **`untype` keeps an enum variant's name.** It dropped the name, so `Outcome.Passed` became `{}` and `Status.NotOwed("no tax")` became `"no tax"`, and a value stored or sent as plain data couldn't be told from another. A variant with no payload now becomes its name (`"Passed"`), and a variant with a payload a Map from its name to the payload (`{NotOwed: "no tax"}`). A record or variant field of an enum type reads that form back, so `Filing(untype(filing))` rebuilds the same value. A `Result` is unchanged: `untype(ok(5))` is `5`. Typed values already survived `::hot::store` as they are, which a test now pins.

## Behaviour changes

- **A second rotation during an overlap answers `409`.** A key keeps one previous secret, so a second rotation used to stop the first old secret at once, before the time the first rotation promised. It now answers `409` `rotation_overlap_running` and changes nothing. To end an overlap early, rotate with `"overlap_seconds": 0`, which is always accepted.
- **Records:** a record given a field of the wrong type is now an Err, where it used to build. Code that built a record with null at a required field, or with a Str for a number, needs the field declared `T?` or the value fixed. Numbers convert as at a parameter, so a `Dec` field given `5` now holds a `Dec`, and `eq(record.amount, 5)` is false: compare with `5.0` or declare the field `Int`.
- **Published packages:** a package's records are checked by the Hot that runs them, so an older `hot.dev/openai` refuses those same responses. Move to openai 1.3.1. In any generated API package, a response whose real data breaks a field's declared type is now an Err rather than a record holding it.
- **`gt`, `lt`, `gte` and `lte` compare a value of a declared type as the number it holds.** With `Money type Dec`, `gt(Money(80.0), 100)` was true and `gt(Money(200.0), Money(80.0))` was false, because the two values were compared as printed text. `Int` types did the same. They now go by the number, and so do `between`, and `where` constraints on such a value, which accepted a `Money` that `gt(%, 0)` should refuse and refused one that `lte(%, 100)` should accept.
- **`gt`, `lt`, `gte` and `lte` give an `Err` for values with no order.** `gt(null, 1)` was true and `gt([10], [9])` was false, from the same comparison of printed text. Comparing a number with `null`, a string or a collection, or two collections, now gives `gt requires numbers`, as `add` does. Like any `Err` it halts when used, and `if` reads it as false, so code that compared a missing field with a number takes the other branch or stops where it went on before. Two strings and two bools order as they did.
- **`sort` and `sort-by` put numbers in order wherever they are.** `Val`'s order ranked every Int before every Dec, so `sort([Money(200), Money(80.5)])` kept that order, as did `sort([[200], [80.5]])`. Numbers now go by value inside other values too, and a value of a declared type sorts among the plain values it reads as, not after them.
- **`untype` on a variant:** code that used `untype` to read a payload now gets a Map with the variant's name: `untype(Due.Days(3))` is `{Days: 3}`, not `3`. Read a payload with `match` or field access. JSON sent with `to-json(untype(value))` changes the same way for any variant inside `value`. Plain data saved by an earlier `untype` holds no variant name, so a record field of an enum type refuses a bare payload.
